name: Prune learnings from build prompts
hypothesis: LEARNINGS.md adds ~2K tokens to every build prompt. Since all actionable patterns are promoted to RULES.md, removing learnings from build prompts will not decrease first-pass rate but will reduce input token usage and iteration cost
change: Remove LEARNINGS.md content from build phase prompt rendering. Keep RULES.md and all other context intact. Learnings remain available in review and retro phases
measurement: Compare over next 50 build iterations: (1) first-pass rate should remain within 2% of 96.7% baseline, (2) avg input tokens should decrease, (3) success rate should remain within 1 std dev of baseline
risk: Some provisional learnings may contain useful context for edge cases not yet promoted to rules. Could cause regression on novel failure patterns
study_summary: Learnings successfully excluded from build prompts (confirmed_learnings=0, recent_learnings=0 in all 30 iterations). However, learnings were only ~2K tokens — <0.3% of total input. Input tokens actually increased 35% (770K → 1.04M) due to model mix shifting to Codex (29/30 iterations). Cost increased 31% ($1.45 → $1.90). Success rate improved from 77.6% to 96.7% but this is attributable to micro-decomposition rules, not the experiment. The hypothesis was wrong: the real cost driver is Codex full-repo context at 1M+ tokens, not prompt content.
